title: Find the biggest folders filling the disk
summary: List the folders that take the most space, one level deep, so you can see what fills the disk. The commands only read information and delete nothing. Folders that only root can read may need sudo.

aliases.text: what folder takes the most space linux
what is eating my disk space linux
linux which folder uses most space
что занимает место на диске linux
какая папка занимает больше всего места linux
диск заполнен linux какие папки занимают место
linux du sort папки по размеру
что съело место на диске linux

prerequisites: Your password, only if the command asks for sudo

steps.explain: Show the size of each folder directly inside the chosen folder, sorted from smallest to largest, and keep the 15 biggest. -x stays on one disk. 2>/dev/null hides 'Permission denied' messages. Read-only, but a big disk can take minutes.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Folder to scan: / for the whole system, or ~ for your home folder

steps.expect: Lines like '4.2G<TAB>/var'. The biggest folders are at the bottom. The last line is FOLDER itself with its total size. Without sudo, folders you cannot read are skipped silently.

alternatives.explain: Use sudo to also read folders that only root can open, such as /root or /var/lib. You are asked for your password. Read-only.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Folder to scan: / for the whole system, or ~ for your home folder

alternatives.expect: The same kind of list. Sizes for root-only folders now appear, so the total for / can be bigger than without sudo.

steps.explain: Look inside the biggest folder from the previous step the same way. Repeat with the biggest subfolder until you find the one that holds most of the data. Read-only.

placeholders.name: BIG_FOLDER
placeholders.description: A folder from the bottom of the previous list, for example /var or ~/Downloads

steps.expect: The same kind of list, now for the subfolders of BIG_FOLDER. The last line is BIG_FOLDER with its total size.

alternatives.explain: Use sudo to read a folder that only root can open, such as /var or /root. You are asked for your password. Read-only.

placeholders.name: BIG_FOLDER
placeholders.description: A folder from the bottom of the previous list, for example /var or ~/Downloads

alternatives.expect: The same kind of list, including subfolders that only root can read.

verify.expect: One line: a size such as 2.3G, a tab, then your home folder path. This confirms the size check works.
